v1.status: v1 complete; v2 normalization fix and history-quadrature experiment awaiting root build
findings: Certified constant-waveform Schwarz has fourth-order temporal convergence but loses badly in CPU cost because elliptic waveform convergence requires many outer sweeps.
Fixed one-sweep constant prediction approaches first order; sigma-only cubic prediction approaches second order; joint U/sigma cubic prediction retains fourth-order smooth behavior.
Four-to-one inner-sweep reduction cuts host cost, but one-inner joint-history mode still loses to RK4 at comparable error on N12.
A second outer sweep and halo2 barely improve state accuracy at higher cost in tested smooth cases.

V1 small-dt compression failures are under investigation as a local residual-normalization error: boundary-driven effective RHS was incorrectly scaled by only volume source. They are not yet evidence of physical instability.
The v1 large-dt compression candidate reaches .08 but is substantially less accurate than RK4 at the same dt.
limits: CPU work probe only; no GPU or complete application speedup measured.
Reduced pseudo1D U4 DGSEM plus lumped continuous LGL closure differs from 2D application spatial discretization.
Stage closure/collocation defects are reported independently; fixed-sweep rows miss the requested strict gates despite accurate smooth endpoints.
First3history steps use fully charged RK4; last refinement pair contains37/77 actual predictor steps, limiting startup masking.
Reference timestep halving at dt.001 preserves displayed state and sigma errors; smallest errors approach FP64 noise.

v2.status: complete: bounded temporal-order, compression, reference-refinement and stability screens
findings: Using the eliminated boundary-driven RHS to scale local patch residuals resolves all previous small-step compression failures; those v1 failures were numerical gate bugs, not physical instability.
Strong RK4 reuses the already exact accepted endpoint closure for k1. Its fields and errors match v1 while reducing global factors from1+5*steps to1+4*steps.

Joint cubic state/sigma history with zero local Picard updates defines an explicit general-linear two-node Gauss flux quadrature, not ADER or a collocation solve. It reaches tf=.04 in smooth and compression cases and tends to fourth-order accuracy.
One local Picard update with joint history tends to fourth order in compression; the smooth case shows approximately fifth-order decay on this particular fixture, which is not a general order claim.
Neither method wins the small CPU probe at equal dt or matched field accuracy: inner0 is roughly1.2x slower with roughly44x compression state error; inner1 roughly2.5x slower with roughly10x error.

Patch methods reduce global factors and estimated factorization FLOPs but increase coefficient assembly, patch solves, and retained storage. All setup, startup, exact endpoint closure and global certificates are charged.
Fixed-sweep closure defects remain above the strict1e-12 stage gate even when final fields converge; these runs must not be reported as certified solutions of instantaneous stage equations.
Global certificates compute the same two transport residuals as the following conservative corrector. A future algebraic reuse could reduce probe overhead; current timing includes both.
Reference timestep halving for compression dt=.001 changes errors by less than a few parts per million.

The longer compression horizon rejects inner0 atdt.004: density/pressure admission fails aftert=.052; atdt.002 current-density correction fails aftert=.102. Atdt.008 it fails the shorter.08 target aftert=.056. RK4 reaches every corresponding horizon.
Inner0 atdt.001 reaches.2 but stateerror1.956e-6 versusRK45.027e-8 and time.03619s versus.02854s. Stop developing this local variant; no speedup winner.

Inner1 reaches.2 atdt.004,.002,.001 with stateerrors3.045e-5,1.932e-6,1.321e-7 and approximatelyfourth-order decay. It costsabout2.7xRK4 with2.6–2.9xstateerror atsame dt; no measured matched-quality gain.
These results support joint temporal history as an accuracy-preserving way to reduce global factors, but do not establish independent element-local ADER or a successful end-to-end tensor engine.
limits: CPU-only reduced pseudo1D full-energy Euler plus lumped continuous LGL IGR; not a complete2D DGSEM or HDG application speedup.
The compression front is smooth but narrow relative to N12 mesh; this is temporal convergence of a fixed semidiscretization, not spatial shock convergence.
Stage closure norm is separate from endpoint sigma field error; RK4 zero stage-defect fields mean no stage certificate was computed.
Global dense factorization baseline at N12 is not the production iterative/preconditioned IGR solve; scaling extrapolation is unsupported.
One timing sample per case; millisecond CPU times have noise. Factor and operation counters are deterministic.

No tensor instructions are measured. The patch solves expose two actual temporal RHS that could map to batched matrix hardware, with eight conservative transport columns, but hardware benefit is unmeasured.
Method times exclude common Problem/LGL basis construction and initial field sampling; manifests record total processwall including these, MPI initialization and the independent reference.
Current-density correction failures after substantial long-horizon evolution are recorded as method failures; the code reports the failing criterion, not an inferred root cause.
A frozen patch factor can require more correction work or fail as state density changes; no fallback or rejected-step retry is implemented in this reduced probe.
